correctness.rationale: For fixed theta the Q-energy gives the stated two-sided time bound. Projecting multiplication by theta twice misses only the path through the first omitted Legendre polynomial, with coefficient a_s squared. Alternating parity yields the two blocks K and -K, with K=(-T+bU)D. The trace telescopes to (-1)^(s-1)b s^2/(4s^2-1); averaging the real parts gives the claimed abscissa bound for every s, including s=1. At s=2 the block has trace -4b/15 and discriminant (14b/15)^2-4/3<0, giving the displayed example. A positive-real-part eigenspace supplies real exponentially growing solutions. The square evaluation matrix at the s nodes, weighted for the probability measure, is orthogonal by degree 2s-2 exactness. It conjugates T and the quadrature U to the nodes and their squares respectively, including the zero node when present. Each block has the same positive energy bounds as the underlying realization. The rank-one identity concerns the theta-squared product matrix; the difference in the full two-component generators has rank two for b>0.
residual_risks: The computation is corroboration only. No claim about all initial conditions, time integration schemes, or finite-time convergence as s grows.
